Keep in mind

  1. Observed anchors. Two category readings were used to determine a compound growth curve.
  2. Activity to visitors. Events per window / events per visitor gives a scenario arrival rate. A combination of browsing duration plus route travel was used to determine relative occupancy.
  3. Spatial placement. Visitors enter a sort of simplified route and browse beside the displays. Staff wander near their assigned categories. The exact positions are only demonstrative.
  4. One reproducible clock. Rebuilding with the same inputs and seed reproduces the same tracks. Both floors advance together.
Assumptions & limitations

Floor allocation was made by the 70/30 assumption. Initial occupants are a synthetic warm start. Browsing duration excludes travel time; no relationship between visitor counts and unique observed customers is claimed. Furniture exclusions and paths are approximate, not a measured navigation map. No queueing, capacity, service outcomes or purchase probability is modelled. Staff movement retains category totals; observed interchangeability is not a measured transition rule.

Growth: P(t) = P₁ × (P₂/P₁)^((t−t₁)/(t₂−t₁)). P is events per observation window, not a point-in-time headcount. Within each model window the arrival rate is constant. Beyond the two anchor windows values are extrapolated. Zero anchors are rejected because this growth model cannot handle them.

Reference: Apple_Singapore_Updated_Study.docx, Orchard observations, 6 November 2026. Staff interaction and demo counts are not used to fabricate service durations. Category “desktop” follows your broad definition including tablets.
